rule: A contract changes only by a new version. The spec, every implementer and the tests change in the same commit, and the change is recorded in decisions.jsonl. tests/run_tests.py checks that every file below carries the current marker.

contracts.what: Normalized conversation JSON and message ids (T3u, T3a, T3a2), and the same ids in Markdown markers.
tests: schema: renderer tags the version and gives every message a unique mid
schema: an unknown version is refused by seed, SSD and telemetry

contracts.what: The handoff file: front matter, sections, states, log line, and the folder's .ledger.json owner and lane settings. @2 (HO-20261101-005): random lane-coded ids (HO-LANE-YYYYMMDD-XXXX), actors with a session (lane#session), steps recorded 'for' another party. Optional touches: (paths, globs or thread URLs) for overlap warnings; readers that don't use it ignore it. @1 files (HO-YYYYMMDD-NNN, no sessions) stay readable and valid.
tests: ledger: prepared -> sent -> acknowledged -> completed, then check
ledger: a handoff from a newer contract version is refused
ledger: @2 needs a session on every actor; the owner needs none

contracts.what: Marking relayed and pasted material: a FROM: first line, FROM: ... END FROM blocks, and >""" pastes.
tests: ssd: a FROM ... END FROM block after your words is stripped from own text
seed: a FROM block inside your message is flagged as a paste, speaker stays you

contracts.what: chat-relay's reply statuses: done (explicit completion signal), unconfirmed (text stopped, no signal), pending.
tests: relay: text that stops changing without a signal is never "done"
relay: explicit ChatGPT completion -> done

contracts.what: Read-only export of a records store: manifest.json (queried sources, counts, time bounds, hashes, filters, redaction policy, exclusions, coverage gaps) and records.jsonl (one record per item, with kind, rid, source_path, source_hash, lane, actor, ts/ts_missing and evidence_class). Reads conversation@1 and handoff@1/@2; changes neither.
tests: export: message round trip from a conversation@1 capture preserves text, ids and order
export: a relayed message is marked relay with its origin, distinct from original speech
export: missing captures, hidden steps, absent timestamps and missing outputs are reported in the manifest
export: a destination inside a public or unconfirmed GitHub repository is refused

contracts.what: What the decision and challenge ledgers say is open, settled, in force or contested, decided once (tools/lifecycle.py) and shared by check_ledgers, status, export, the MCP server and the cockpit. A supersedes takes effect only from a settled line (adopted closes any earlier decision; rejected and superseded settle a proposal only and cannot retire an adopted decision); a proposed line is a proposed replacement; a resolves only from a resolved or accepted-risk line; self, forward and unknown references are problems and take no effect; more than one effective closer is a conflict, kept, not collapsed. Applicability of an adopted decision: standing ('adopted, no structured supersession found'), superseded, revoked (revokes), expired or not yet effective (effective_from/until); amends (an id or {id, clauses}) records a partial amendment. Export records gain applicability, closed_by, proposed_replacements, amended_by, conflict, transition_problems (decisions) and open, closed_by, conflict (challenges); in_force follows these rules. Adopting a proposal replaces what it proposed to replace; a closing and a revoking line on one record is a conflict; an amendment lapses with what it amends; effective dates are evaluated against the ledger's latest date by every reader; check_ledgers reports invalid transitions on earlier lines as warnings. export and mcp stay @1 with this deviation recorded in docs/lifecycle.md.
tests: lifecycle: the six review reproductions and the other fixture cases resolve as specified
lifecycle: check_ledgers refuses exactly the cases with a transition that takes no effect
lifecycle: status, export, the MCP server and the cockpit show the same open items and in-force decisions
lifecycle: a transition that takes no effect on an earlier line is a warning, so later appends still work; a new one is refused

contracts.what: Read-only static control surface over a records store: DIR/index.html (one self-contained page: Choices, Topology, Budget, Run/Drift and the other v0.4 surfaces) and DIR/cockpit.json (the data it was built from). Choices compose paste-ready ledger_append / handoff set lines and write nothing (DEC-019). Reads decisions, challenges, handoff@1/@2, threads.md and conversation@1 through the export@1 readers, plus governance/budget.jsonl; changes none of them. Deterministic; no clock is read (the newest record, the records revision and its commit and fetch times are shown, not today). @2 (HO-RK-20261105-VZH4): each choice says what it asks (the proposer's optional `ask`, else a summary labelled derived), what cites it and waits on it, its age, and whether it may be overtaken (later citations; opt-in build-time PR states); Amend and Clarify compose ledger lines (an amending adopted line; an open question challenge addressed to the proposer); Inquire copies an off-record prompt; Questions lists open questions. @3 (HO-RK-20261105-SWK5): a Pull requests surface rendering governance/pr-state.jsonl (relay-kit/prs@1): each PR's What / Why / How / Authorized verbatim with who wrote it (an agent's Author: line is tagged as not the owner's), missing sections, reviews with their family and whether one is from another family than the author, CI, and read times; PR states for the overtaken check come from that file, so --pr-state only fills gaps. --theme FILE (known colour variables and font lists only; an optional light scheme with a toggle) and --landing SURFACE. The page still fetches and writes nothing. Additive: nothing in @2 changed meaning. @4 (HO-RK-20261105-8DTW): reads the ledgers through relay-kit/lifecycle@1 (a proposal leaves Choices only when a settled line closes it; a proposed replacement is shown on its card; transitions that take no effect or conflict are listed on Review); every composed decision or challenge line carries --expect ID=STATE@HASH (and one for what a proposal replaces) so ledger_append refuses it, with what changed, once the item has moved on; the header shows the records' revision, commit time and last fetch (aged in the browser) apart from the newest record. Nothing from @3 was removed.
tests: cockpit: Choices lists exactly the proposed decision, the owner-waiting handoff and the open challenge
cockpit: a composed ledger line parses as JSON with the referenced id and the chosen status, and passes the ledger check
cockpit: --content metadata leaves out decision, challenge and handoff bodies (ids and states only)
cockpit: a destination inside a public GitHub repository or inside the records is refused
cockpit: two runs give byte-identical output and leave the records untouched
cockpit: a composed line pasted unedited is refused by ledger_append (its <<REQUIRED placeholders fail the ledger check)
cockpit: Run commitments count only authorized handoffs in progress; prepared or unauthorized ones are pending
cockpit: only an adopted decision with delegates_to draws a recorded delegation edge
cockpit: every choice says what it asks; the proposer's ask is shown as theirs, anything else is labelled derived
cockpit: Amend and Clarify compose ledger lines that pass the check once filled in, and are refused while placeholders remain
cockpit: Inquire is off the record: no command, no ledger line, only a prompt naming the item
cockpit: Pull requests renders each PR's sections verbatim and escaped, with who wrote it and what is missing
cockpit: an agent-written PR is tagged as not written by the owner; one with no Author line says so
cockpit: --content metadata shows which PR sections exist but none of their text
cockpit: PR states for overtaken checks come from pr-state.jsonl without any network lookup
cockpit: a theme can set only known variables to colours or font lists; anything else is refused
cockpit: a theme with a light block adds a light scheme and a toggle; without --theme the page is unchanged dark
cockpit: --landing opens the page on the named surface; an unknown surface is refused
cockpit: merged or closed pull requests older than the reader's window are counted, not listed
lifecycle: the cockpit composes Accept, Reject, Amend and Close-as-overtaken with --expect, and shows a proposed replacement on the card
lifecycle: a composed line with --expect is refused, with what changed, once its item has been settled

contracts.what: governance/pr-state.jsonl, append-only, written by relay-kit prs at build time from GitHub (gh CLI or a token): a 'pr' line when a pull request's state changed since its last line (repo, number, url, title, state open|closed|merged, draft, author, author_line from the body's Author: line, times, base, head, reviews [{by, verdict, at, signed, stated}], ci {state success|failure|pending|none, failing}, body_sections {what, why, how, authorized} verbatim with HTML comments removed, missing, truncated) and a 'fetch' line per run (ts, via, repos, ok, failed, since_days, prs_seen, appended). Repositories from handoffs/.ledger.json 'repos' or --repo. The one GitHub reader for pull requests: the Cockpit and other readers read the file. @2 (HO-RK-20261105-TXRM step 1): pull requests are read through tools/github.py, the kit's read-only client for pull-request reads (GET only; pagination; retries with backoff; rate-limit waits or refusal with the reset time; one fetch per path per run; optional ETag cache). A pr line gains `unread` (reviews or ci that couldn't be read: missing is not zero; ci state 'unknown'); the fetch line gains `coverage` per repository (what was asked, listed, more_available, re-read open PRs, PRs read, partial reads), `revisions` (default branch and pushed_at) and `client` (requests, retries, waits, cache hits, rate limit left, first/last request time). @1 lines stay readable.
tests: prs: body sections are kept verbatim; missing and comment-only sections are listed as missing
prs: an unchanged PR appends no new line; a changed one appends one, and every run appends a fetch line
prs: a failing repository is recorded in the fetch line and the others are still read
prs: it writes only governance/pr-state.jsonl and never rewrites a line
prs: CI state from check runs and statuses; reviews keep the verdict stated in their body
prs: repositories come from .ledger.json repos or --repo; anything not OWNER/NAME is refused
prs: a PR last recorded open is read again however old, so a closed one never stays open
prs: appending to a file without a final newline doesn't join two lines
github: pages walks pages until the limit or a short page, and says whether more were available
github: network errors and 5xx are retried with backoff; other errors and exhausted retries are refused with the status
github: a rate limit waits for the reset when it is short, and is refused with the reset time when it isn't
github: a path is fetched once per run; with a cache folder an unchanged resource is revalidated by its ETag
github: the gh transport only ever sends GET, and parses status and headers from its output
prs: what was asked for and what came back is recorded per repository; unreadable reviews or CI are unread, not none
prs: a PR that can't be read again is a partial read, not a failed repository; an unread part keeps its last value and adds no line

contracts.what: governance/budget.jsonl, append-only: @1's ts, actor, window, tokens_in, tokens_out (and optional agents, note) plus @2's id (or a content-hash id for older lines), method (measured | proxy | estimate; required on new lines, 'unlabelled' for older ones), interval_start/end, includes_children {included, ids}, correction_of (an earlier line, same window: the replaced line is never summed with its correction and its use keeps the replaced line's time; two corrections of one line are a reported conflict, the later counting), metric_version, scope and source. Read through tools/budget.py by every reader; written by relay-kit budget-append. tokens_detail {input, output, cache_write, cache_read, by_model} keeps cache reads apart. relay-kit usage-ingest (tools/usage_ingest.py) turns a Claude Code session's local logs into one line per session: measured when the logs are complete, an estimate marked complete:false (a lower bound, with log_coverage) when compacted or late (message ids counted once across main and subagent logs; costUSD unused; re-ingesting appends a correction; no paths in the line).
tests: budget: a correction replaces the line it names; the two are never summed
budget: a parent that includes its children's use isn't counted with them
budget: new lines must say how they were measured; malformed @2 fields are refused
budget: two corrections of one line are a conflict, reported; only the later one counts
budget: older lines without a method count as 'unlabelled', never as measured
budget: a correction is counted at the time of the line it replaces, so relabelling never moves use into this week
budget: children are followed through corrections, inclusion is inherited, and self, later, cross-window and cyclic references are reported and ignored
budget: the same reading appended twice gets two ids; duplicate ids in the file are reported and both lines read; a corrected line can't be corrected again
usage: one measured line per session; a message split over several log lines counts once; cache reads stay apart
usage: ingesting a session again appends a correction, so the cockpit counts it once
usage: the line carries counts and the session id only: no file paths or folder names
usage: a compacted log, or one starting well after its session did, gives an estimate marked incomplete, never a measurement
usage: a re-run that shows less than before is refused; duplicate session lines are refused; unidentified usage lines and zone-less times aren't counted

contracts.what: A derived view (tools/telemetry.py, relay-kit telemetry), rebuilt from the records and never stored in them: compute_consumption, delivery_throughput, lead_time, review_burden, post_merge_remediation (14 and 30 days, mature cohorts only), surviving_changes, human_intervention, idea_to_completed_handoff_latency (DEC-162's progress proxy: a recorded 'Idea captured: <time>' in a handoff's Task or Context section to its first completed step; measured only when both exist; invalid, future or reversed markers excluded by name), measurement_coverage and coordination_loss, each with a frozen definition, a version, a measured/proxy/estimate/derived/unknown label, --lane and --content metadata as the cockpit applies them, distributions (median, p90, n) and 'unknown' with a reason in place of zero. No composite score, no targets. The cockpit's Review surface shows it.
tests: telemetry: every metric carries its definition, version and label; with no records each says unknown, never zero
telemetry: lead time and review burden are distributions from pr-state; abandoned PRs are counted apart
telemetry: remediation is counted only over cohorts old enough; only a fix or revert wording right before this repository's reference counts
telemetry: corrections and child runs are applied before compute is summed; a malformed line is counted invalid, as the cockpit counts it, and breaks nothing
telemetry: the cockpit's Review panel shows each metric with its label and definition, no score or target, at the page's as of
telemetry: the view is derived and is never written into the records
telemetry: --content metadata reads no free text (claims and remediation are unknown); --lane keeps other lanes' handoffs and sessions out
telemetry: a time after the last pull-request read doesn't move as_of; it is flagged instead

telemetry: capture latency is measured only from a marker in a handoff's Task or Context and a completed step; markers elsewhere, invalid, future or reversed are excluded by name, other lanes left out, metadata unknown, never zero

contracts.what: Read-only MCP server over a records store, JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio or Streamable HTTP (POST /mcp, JSON back; GET 405; no SSE, no session), protocol revisions 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 (any other gets -32022 with the supported list, as an HTTP 400 when it arrives in the MCP-Protocol-Version header): the tool names and arguments, relaykit:// resource URIs, the result envelope (schema, evidence_class as in export@1, provenance 'read from <path> at records sha256:<hash>', content_level, notice) and the --content metadata policy, the default over HTTP. HTTP binds loopback only, requires Authorization: Bearer <token> with the token read from a file (401 otherwise, with no record content), refuses non-loopback Origins (403), and logs method, tool and timing, never bodies. Both transports run one handler. No tool writes to the records (DEC-019).
tests: mcp: initialize handshake, tools/list and ping over stdio, for each supported protocol version
mcp: a 2026-07-28 or unknown protocol version gets -32022 with the supported list, never a silent fallback
mcp: every read tool answers with evidence_class and a provenance line naming the records hash
mcp: with --content metadata no tool or resource returns record text, and text filters are refused
mcp: read tools change nothing in the records, and instruction-like record text isn't acted on
mcp: malformed JSON-RPC gets a proper error and the server keeps serving
mcp: the HTTP transport answers every request the stdio transport does, with the same body
mcp: HTTP requests without the bearer token get 401 and no body from the records; GET gets 405
mcp: a batch over HTTP is answered as a batch; notifications alone get 202
mcp: the HTTP server binds loopback only and takes its token from a file, never a flag value
mcp: unauthenticated idle connections cannot exceed the configured worker bound
mcp: idle headers and stalled authenticated bodies expire within finite connection deadlines
mcp: every well-formed unsupported HTTP method is authenticated and logged
mcp: control characters in RPC methods and paths cannot forge extra request-log lines
mcp: early authentication and routing refusals close the connection before any pipelined body
mcp: concurrent HTTP initialization cannot overwrite another request's negotiated revision
mcp: the hardened smoke client passes all checks against a synthetic authenticated server
mcp: transfer encodings and duplicate content lengths are refused before reading a body
mcp-smoke: no redirect status or method forwards a bearer to another origin
mcp-smoke: even same-origin redirects are refused without a global opener change
mcp-smoke: environment proxies cannot capture a loopback bearer
mcp-smoke: response bodies have a bounded read on success and HTTP failure
mcp-smoke: plaintext DNS hosts, userinfo, foreign schemes and ambiguous URLs are refused before I/O
mcp-smoke: HTTPS and literal IPv4/IPv6 loopback HTTP use a private no-proxy opener
mcp-smoke: real local HTTP errors and malformed response bodies never reach CLI output
mcp-smoke: valid results print fixed check labels, vetted state and numeric counts, never the URL
mcp-smoke: failed checks never print bodies, headers, tool names, schemas or arbitrary count data
mcp-smoke: malformed JSON containers and nested fields fail safely without tracebacks
mcp-smoke: counts have fixed names and bounded nonnegative integers, not arbitrary JSON
mcp-smoke: summary, counts and envelope scalar type confusion cannot escape validation
mcp-smoke: connection and protocol exceptions produce fixed diagnostics without secrets
mcp-smoke: invalid arguments and unreadable or invalid token files never echo paths or token text
mcp-smoke: duplicate JSON keys cannot hide data in either unauthorized response or nested results
